evals.fixture: a git repo with .dev/discount-pricing/plan.md and no task_N.md files
assertions: The user is asked to run to-tasks first rather than the plan being implemented straight from plan.md
to-tasks is not invoked automatically
No implementation code is written

evals.fixture: a git repo with .dev/{plan-name}/plan.md and task_1.md, task_2.md (task_2 depends on task_1), each with a small independently-verifiable behavior, acceptance criteria tagged [unit]
assertions: Both task_1 and task_2 are implemented, not just the first one
Task_2's work is attempted only after task_1's is committed (dependency order respected)
The two tasks are not launched concurrently, since task_2 depends on task_1
Tests are behavior-named (e.g. "applies a discount") rather than test1/test2, cover cases beyond the happy path, and no assertion recomputes the expected value the way the implementation does
The user is not asked about running to-review after task_1 finishes - no review prompt appears until both tasks are done
Each task gets its own commit on the current branch (at least 2 commits)
.dev/{plan-name}/implementation-notes.md is created and has one entry per task
After both tasks are done, the user is asked to run to-review rather than a review panel being launched automatically

evals.fixture: a git repo with .dev/{plan-name}/plan.md and task_1.md, task_2.md, task_3.md where task_1 and task_2 both have 'Depends on: None' and disjoint Files touched, task_3 depends on both; criteria tagged [unit] and [integration]
assertions: task_1 and task_2 are launched as subagents in a single message so they run concurrently
task_3 is not started until task_1 and task_2 are both committed
The subagents do not commit, stage, or otherwise touch git state - the orchestrator makes the commits
The subagents do not write to implementation-notes.md themselves; the orchestrator appends each entry
The subagents are told not to launch the app or run e2e criteria
Each task's self-validation commands are re-run by the orchestrator rather than the subagent's claim being taken at face value
Three commits exist, one per task, in dependency-respecting order

evals.fixture: a git repo with a tiny Node CLI (bin/cli.js exposing a `total` command over a cart file) and .dev/cart-total/plan.md plus task_1.md whose acceptance criteria are tagged [unit] Given a cart with items When totaling Then the sum is correct, [integration] Given the CLI command When invoked with a cart file Then it reads and totals it, and [e2e] Given a user runs the built CLI against a real cart file When it exits Then it prints the correct total - kind: non-frontend
assertions: A unit test exists for the totaling business logic in isolation, no process spawned
An integration test exists that exercises the CLI command against a real (not mocked) cart-reading path
The e2e criterion is proven by actually invoking the built CLI as a subprocess against a real cart file, not by re-running the unit/integration tests
The e2e run uses a mocked, seeded, deterministic environment - no real external service or production data is touched
The e2e pass happens after the task is committed, not interleaved with the unit/integration cycles
.dev/cart-total/implementation-notes.md exists and references what was done for the task

A cart-total-e2e-report.html is written locally under ~/tmp/{project-slug}/reports/, kind is non-frontend, and it contains a dataModelState entry with real before/after values rather than a screenshot
No screenshot or dataUri field is fabricated for a kind: non-frontend report
The report is opened in the browser (open/xdg-open) and published via the Artifact tool, with both the local path and the returned URL reported

evals.fixture: a git repo like e2e-cli-mocked-env, but the CLI has a latent formatting bug that only shows when the built binary runs end to end, so the first e2e capture fails
assertions: The failing e2e scenario is diagnosed and fixed rather than reported as an accepted failure or a limitation
The fix is driven by a new failing test at the layer that can catch it, not only by patching until the e2e passes
The scenario is re-run and re-captured after the fix, not flipped to pass with the original capture
The final report's summary counts match the scenarios array and reflect the passing re-run
The user is asked to run to-review only after the e2e run is green
